CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who presents with right elbow pain sustained approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children. He reports being struck multiple times with a lacrosse stick by his 13-year-old son during play. The pain began acutely during the game. He describes the pain as sharp, localized to the tip of the elbow, and radiating down the forearm. Pain is exacerbated with any elbow movement. He attempted over-the-counter ibuprofen a few days ago with some subjective improvement. Denies fall or recall of direct impact, though acknowledges potential lacrosse stick contact during play.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain. No other systemic symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes mellitus type 2
3. Systolic ejection murmur (known, grade 2/6)

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily
2. Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient has two children ages 13 and 10. Participates in recreational lacrosse with his children. Follows Mediterranean-style diet with low sodium intake; avoids adding salt to food. Family follows similar dietary pattern. Reports improved dietary adherence recently after falling off during the pandemic.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 150/90 (elevated)
General: Well-appearing
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur present (known)
Abdomen: Benign, no pain
Right Elbow: Mild swelling and bruising noted; tenderness to palpation over olecranon region; mild pain with flexion and extension; full range of motion maintained

RESULTS
Right elbow X-ray: No fracture, no bony abnormality, normal
Blood glucose: Patient reports occasional readings 80-100 mg/dL when checked
A1C: Ordered, pending results

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right elbow contusion - Secondary to blunt trauma from lacrosse stick. X-ray negative for fracture. Prescribed ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily for pain and swelling. Ice 3 times daily for 20 minutes per session. Recommend rest from lacrosse for next couple of weeks to allow healing. May resume activities once healed.

2. Hypertension - Currently on lisinopril 20 mg daily. Blood pressure elevated today at 150/90, likely white coat syndrome. Patient demonstrates good compliance with low-sodium Mediterranean diet. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Encourage continued dietary adherence.

3. Diabetes mellitus type 2 - Currently on metformin 500 mg daily. Blood glucose control adequate with readings 80-100 mg/dL. Ordered A1C to assess glycemic control and determine if dose adjustment needed. Continue metformin 500 mg daily pending A1C results. Will adjust medication if necessary after results reviewed.
